If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (alternating 0.3–1.0) in the last 5 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecast to smooth volatility.  
If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.3) across 10+ days, apply a 3–5% downward correction to late-horizon (16–30 days) forecast to reflect persistent bearish momentum.  
If sentiment is uniformly high (≥0.7) across 10+ days, apply a 2–4% upward correction to late-horizon (16–30 days) forecast to reflect sustained bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) in the last 5 days with no clear trend, apply a 1–2% neutral adjustment to mid-horizon (8–15 days) to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
